Question_text: Sodium percarbonate is often used to remove stains from clothing. It is a white solid with the formula Na2CO3.xH2O2. When the solid dissolves in water, it produces a solution containing sodium carbonate and hydrogen peroxide. P is a solution containing 7.85g of Na2CO3.xH2O2 in 1.00dm³ of solution. Q is 0.100mol/dm³ hydrochloric acid. You are to determine the value of x in the formula Na2CO3.xH2O2 by titrating the sodium carbonate in P with Q. Na2CO3 + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H2O + CO2
Topic: 3.3 The mole and the Avogadro constant
